VIDEO.title: A Satanic Pattern Is Spreading Through Christian Circles
VIDEO.series: The Book of Romans, Every Word (playlist of 28 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Romans 16 · Episode 28 (#28 of 28 in the playlist, the last)
SUMMARY: The teacher opens the final episode: the chapter we skip most may be the one we need right now, because buried in Romans 16 is a warning about deceptive voices, division and Satan himself. He reads Romans 16: Phoebe commended (16:1-2); greetings to Prisca and Aquila, the church in their house, and many others (16:3-16); a warning about those who cause divisions (16:17-18); be wise in what is good (16:19); the God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet (16:20); greetings from Timothy, Tertius, Gaius, Erastus and others (16:21-23); the closing doxology (16:25-27).

Observations: the names are real servants, households, co-workers and probably several house church networks, concrete examples of what the gospel produces. Prisca and Aquila also appear in Acts 18, 1 Corinthians 16 and 2 Timothy 4: a ministry-minded couple who risked their necks. Phoebe is a diakonos (servant or deacon) and a patron; the teacher thinks Leon Morris is probably right that she held an official role. Prisca is named before her husband, which may suggest status or prominence. Paul's honors vary: co-workers, firstfruits, women who labored, fellow prisoners, a mother to Paul.

The warning (16:17-18) should be read in light of Romans 14-15: those who create stumbling blocks undermine the welcome and unity Paul has urged. 'Wise in what is good and innocent in what is evil' (16:19) sounds close to Jesus in Matthew 10:16. The doxology (16:25-27) is balanced and concentric, and bookends Romans 1:1-5: gospel, Jesus Messiah, prophetic Scriptures, nations, obedience of faith, glory to God.

Old Testament background: stumbling blocks (Leviticus 19:14) and priests who caused many to stumble by their instruction (Malachi 2:8); a faint echo of Genesis 3:6 in appetite, smooth speech and the naive led away; the first gospel promise (Genesis 3:15) applied to the church in 16:20; God who strengthens (Isaiah 41:10; Psalms 18, 29, 89; Isaiah 40); the mystery revealed (Daniel 2:19-22; Deuteronomy 29:29; Amos 3:7; Isaiah 48); the nations blessed through Abraham (Genesis 12:3; Psalm 67; Isaiah 49:6; Malachi 1:11). The Gentile mission was not plan B; it was the plan.

Welcome or avoid (15:7; 16:17)? Paul is not contradicting himself: welcome the sincere brother or sister who sees things differently; avoid the divisive deceiver. Christian unity is not naive tolerance. Not every disagreement is satanic, but division fueled by deception and self-interest serves Satan's purposes. The church's witness is tied to its unity (John 17:21-23).
The lesson: 'Christian unity does not require tolerating divisive deceivers. It requires guarding the unity Christ created by refusing those who tear it apart.'
QUOTES: Christian unity does not require tolerating divisive deceivers. It requires guarding the unity Christ created by refusing those who tear it apart.
The algorithm doesn't care if Christians become holy. It only cares that they stay engaged.
Online attention is a form of hospitality.

method.p: In Romans 16 list every person named and the honor Paul gives each (fellow worker, beloved, labored, approved). Then lay Romans 1:1-5 beside 16:25-27 and mark the shared words: gospel, prophets, Scriptures, Gentiles, obedience of faith.

And the God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.

src.text: Now I commend to you our sister Phoebe, who is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea; that you receive her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and that you help her in whatever matter she may have need of you; for she herself has also been a benefactor of many, and of myself as well.

lines.text: Paul uses diakonos, the word behind 'deacon'; some translations say servant, others deacon or deaconess. The term can be broad, but given the formal commendation and her role as prostatis, a patron or benefactor, the teacher thinks Leon Morris is probably right that she held an official ministry role.

left.text: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus, who for my life risked their own necks, to whom not only do I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles; also greet the church that is in their house.

right.text: and he began to speak out boldly in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately.

lines.text: They also appear in 1 Corinthians 16 and 2 Timothy 4: married co-workers who discipled others, opened their home to churches, and risked themselves for the gospel. Naming the wife first was unusual; it may suggest higher social status, greater prominence in ministry, or that she was especially well known. We shouldn't overstate it, but it is probably not an accident.

src.text: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and my fellow prisoners, who are outstanding to the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.

lines.text: The household of Aristobulus, the household of Narcissus, 'the brothers with them', 'all the saints who are with them': these are clusters of believers, probably different house churches. Paul's honors vary: Epaenetus the first convert from Asia, Mary who labored, Andronicus and Junia fellow prisoners, Rufus's mother 'and mine' (16:13).

left.text: But as for you, you have turned aside from the way; you have caused many to stumble by the instruction; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi,” says Yahweh of hosts.

right.text: Now I urge you, brothers, to keep your eye on those who cause dissensions and stumblings contrary to the teaching which you learned, and turn away from them.

lines.text: The Greek skandala can mean stumbling blocks, snares or traps, spiritual tripwires in the path of God's people. Behind it stands 'nor place a stumbling block before the blind' (Leviticus 19:14). Read it in light of Romans 14:13 and 15:1, 7; Paul does not detail the error, so we shouldn't over-specify it.

left.text: Then the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was desirable to make one wise, so she took from its fruit and ate; and she gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.

right.text: For such men are slaves, not of our Lord Christ but of their own stomach, and by their smooth and flattering speech they deceive the hearts of the unsuspecting.

lines.text: The teacher does not claim Paul is consciously alluding to Genesis 3:6, but the pattern is familiar: appetite, deceptive speech, the naive led away from obedience. And 16:19 sounds close to Jesus: 'be shrewd as serpents and innocent as doves' (Matthew 10:16). Believers must not be gullible, nor become corrupt.

left.text: And I will put enmity / Between you and the woman, / And between your seed and her seed; / He shall bruise you on the head, / And you shall bruise him on the heel.”

right.text: And the God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.

lines.text: The seed of the woman is ultimately fulfilled in Jesus Christ crushing the serpent's head. Paul intensifies the image: God will crush Satan under the feet of His church. Divisive deception is serpent work, and God's victory is displayed through the church's gospel-centered obedience and unity.

left.text: ‘Do not fear, for I am with you; / Do not anxiously look about you, for I am your God. / I will make you mighty, surely I will help you; / Surely I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.’

right.text: Now to Him who is able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery which has been kept secret for long ages past,

lines.text: The promise was spoken to Israel; because Gentiles have been grafted in, believers can rightly receive the comfort of God's strengthening presence. See also Psalms 18:32, 29:11 and 89:21, and Isaiah 40:29-31.

left.text: He reveals the deep and hidden things; / He knows what is in the darkness, / And the light dwells with Him.

right.text: but now is manifested, and by the Scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the eternal God, has been made known to all the Gentiles, leading to obedience of faith;

lines.text: 'Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a night vision' (Daniel 2:19). A mystery is not a puzzle humans solve but a divine secret God reveals. 'The secret things belong to Yahweh our God' (Deuteronomy 29:29); see also Amos 3:7 and Isaiah 48:6-7.

left.text: through whom we received grace and apostleship for the obedience of faith among all the Gentiles for the sake of His name,

right.text: to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, be the glory forever. Amen.

lines.text: The doxology is balanced and concentric (the teacher outlines it A-B-C-C-B-A without claiming a formal chiasm) and mirrors Romans 1:1-5. The Gentile mission is what the Scriptures always pointed toward: 'in you all the families of the earth will be blessed' (Genesis 12:3); see Psalm 67, Isaiah 49:6 and Malachi 1:11.

BACKGROUND.p: There were no church buildings; believers met in homes. Paul greets several groups, which suggests a network of house churches across the city rather than a single congregation.
Letters traveled by trusted carriers, and Phoebe may have carried Romans. Paul dictated to a scribe, and Tertius adds his own greeting (16:22).

BACKGROUND.h: Claudius and the return to Rome
BACKGROUND.p: Claudius had expelled Jews from Rome (Acts 18:2), probably around AD 49. By the time Paul writes, Prisca and Aquila are back, and Jewish-background believers have returned to churches that had grown more Gentile in the meantime.

DEBATES.p: Diakonos can mean servant in general or name an office. Some, like Leon Morris and the video, think Phoebe held a recognized role in the church at Cenchrea; others read it as a description of her service.

Most now read Junia as a woman's name. The phrase can mean 'outstanding among the apostles' (counting them as apostles in a broad sense, as Chrysostom did) or 'well known to the apostles', as the video's translation and the LSB's 'outstanding to the apostles' allow.

Manuscripts place it in different spots: after 16:23, after 14:23, after 15:33, or in more than one place. Chrysostom's text had it after chapter 14, where he preaches on it in Homily 27. Most modern translations print it at the end.

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: The video says Luke, like Paul, names Priscilla before her husband in Acts 18. Luke does so in 18:18 and 18:26, but 18:2 has 'Aquila... and his wife Priscilla', and Paul himself writes 'Aquila and Prisca' in 1 Corinthians 16:19. The pattern is real but not uniform.
The video's reading of 16:7 says Andronicus and Junia are 'well known to the apostles'; the LSB has 'outstanding to the apostles'. The wording is debated (see Where scholars differ).

QUESTIONS: What does the list of names in Romans 16 show about what the gospel produces?
How do you tell a sincere brother who disagrees from a divisive deceiver?
What voices are you giving access to your mind and community?
What fruit does the content you consume produce in you?
How are you guarding the garden of your church, to work it and keep it?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: Paul did not write with social media in mind, but the internet did not invent division, self-interest or flattering speech; it amplifies and rewards them. First-century influencers moved through house churches, patronage circles and traveling teachers; today it is clips, podcasts, posts and comment sections: a different method, the same spiritual pattern. 'The algorithm doesn't care if Christians become holy. It only cares that they stay engaged.' Not every online critic is wrong: ask whether a voice is faithful, careful, accountable and aiming at repentance and restoration, or self-serving, flattering and faction-making. Watch for language like 'only I am telling you the truth', 'every church is corrupt', 'share this before it gets taken down'. Jesus says false teachers are known by their fruits (Matthew 7:15-20). The teacher is accountable to his local church, pastor and discipleship group, and asks the same of others. Online attention is a form of hospitality, so sometimes obedience means unsubscribing, not sharing, not joining the comment war. He keeps social media off his phone. His Romans 16 test for any voice, including his: Are they anchored in Scripture and careful with it? Do they build up the church? Do they show self-interest or need enemies? Are they accountable? What fruit does their content produce in me?
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): run the video's Romans 16 test on the three voices you listen to most this week, and write down the fruit each one produces in you. Then thank God by name for three people in your own church, as Paul does in 16:1-16.

3. Romans 16:20; Genesis 3:15: Satan crushed under your feet
   Yahweh God (Genesis 3:15, LSB): "And I will put enmity / Between you and the woman, / And between your seed and her seed; / He shall bruise you on the head, / And you shall bruise him on the heel.”"
   Paul (Romans 16:20, LSB): "And the God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you."
   (video) The seed of the woman is ultimately fulfilled in Jesus Christ crushing the serpent's head. Paul intensifies the image: God will crush Satan under the feet of His church. Divisive deception is serpent work, and God's victory is displayed through the church's gospel-centered obedience and unity.

## To the only wise God
1. Romans 16:25; Isaiah 41:10: Able to strengthen you
   Isaiah (Isaiah 41:10, LSB): "‘Do not fear, for I am with you; / Do not anxiously look about you, for I am your God. / I will make you mighty, surely I will help you; / Surely I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.’"
   Paul (Romans 16:25, LSB): "Now to Him who is able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery which has been kept secret for long ages past,"
   (video) The promise was spoken to Israel; because Gentiles have been grafted in, believers can rightly receive the comfort of God's strengthening presence. See also Psalms 18:32, 29:11 and 89:21, and Isaiah 40:29-31.
2. Romans 16:25-26; Daniel 2:19-22: The mystery revealed
   Daniel (Daniel 2:22, LSB): "He reveals the deep and hidden things; / He knows what is in the darkness, / And the light dwells with Him."
   Paul (Romans 16:26, LSB): "but now is manifested, and by the Scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the eternal God, has been made known to all the Gentiles, leading to obedience of faith;"
   (video) 'Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a night vision' (Daniel 2:19). A mystery is not a puzzle humans solve but a divine secret God reveals. 'The secret things belong to Yahweh our God' (Deuteronomy 29:29); see also Amos 3:7 and Isaiah 48:6-7. (Daniel 2:19; Deuteronomy 29:29)
3. Romans 16:25-27; 1:1-5; Genesis 12:3: The bookends of Romans
   Paul (Romans 1:5, LSB): "through whom we received grace and apostleship for the obedience of faith among all the Gentiles for the sake of His name,"
   Paul (Romans 16:27, LSB): "to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, be the glory forever. Amen."
   (video) The doxology is balanced and concentric (the teacher outlines it A-B-C-C-B-A without claiming a formal chiasm) and mirrors Romans 1:1-5. The Gentile mission is what the Scriptures always pointed toward: 'in you all the families of the earth will be blessed' (Genesis 12:3); see Psalm 67, Isaiah 49:6 and Malachi 1:11. (Genesis 12:3)

## Key people
- Phoebe: A servant (diakonos) of the church at Cenchrea and a benefactor of many (16:1-2). [Background] Cenchrea was Corinth's eastern port (Acts 18:18).
- Prisca (Priscilla) and Aquila: Fellow workers who risked their necks for Paul; a church met in their house (16:3-5). [Background] Expelled from Rome under Claudius, they met Paul in Corinth (Acts 18:2).
- Andronicus and Junia: Paul's kinsmen and fellow prisoners, in Christ before him (16:7). [Background] Chrysostom read Junia as a woman honored with the name of apostle (see Early witnesses).
- Tertius: Named among the final greetings (16:22). [Background] The scribe who wrote the letter down as Paul dictated (16:22).
- Timothy: Paul's fellow worker, sending greetings (16:21). [Background] Paul's younger co-worker (Acts 16:1-3).
- Satan: The God of peace will soon crush him under the church's feet (16:20). [Background] The adversary; Genesis 3 pictures the serpent's deception.

## Places [Background]
- Rome (named in the video): House churches greeted by name (16:3-16).
- Corinth (named in the video): Where Paul wrote; Gaius hosted the church and Erastus was city treasurer (16:23).
- Cenchrea (named in the video): Phoebe's church, Corinth's eastern port (16:1).
- Ephesus: Chief city of Asia, where Epaenetus came from and Prisca and Aquila hosted a church (1 Corinthians 16:19).

## Key terms
- Diakonos: Servant, minister; the word behind 'deacon' (16:1).
- Patron (prostatis): Benefactor, supporter (16:2).
- Skandalon: Stumbling block, snare, trap (16:17).
- Protoevangelium: The 'first gospel', the promise of Genesis 3:15 that the woman's seed would bruise the serpent's head.
- Mystery: A divine secret God reveals, not a puzzle humans solve (16:25; Daniel 2).
- Doxology: A closing ascription of glory to God (16:25-27).

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- House churches in Rome: There were no church buildings; believers met in homes. Paul greets several groups, which suggests a network of house churches across the city rather than a single congregation.
- Letter carriers and scribes: Letters traveled by trusted carriers, and Phoebe may have carried Romans. Paul dictated to a scribe, and Tertius adds his own greeting (16:22).
- Claudius and the return to Rome: Claudius had expelled Jews from Rome (Acts 18:2), probably around AD 49. By the time Paul writes, Prisca and Aquila are back, and Jewish-background believers have returned to churches that had grown more Gentile in the meantime.

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Phoebe: servant or deacon? (16:1) Diakonos can mean servant in general or name an office. Some, like Leon Morris and the video, think Phoebe held a recognized role in the church at Cenchrea; others read it as a description of her service.
- Junia and the apostles (16:7) Most now read Junia as a woman's name. The phrase can mean 'outstanding among the apostles' (counting them as apostles in a broad sense, as Chrysostom did) or 'well known to the apostles', as the video's translation and the LSB's 'outstanding to the apostles' allow.
- Where does the doxology belong? (16:25-27) Manuscripts place it in different spots: after 16:23, after 14:23, after 15:33, or in more than one place. Chrysostom's text had it after chapter 14, where he preaches on it in Homily 27. Most modern translations print it at the end.

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- The video says Luke, like Paul, names Priscilla before her husband in Acts 18. Luke does so in 18:18 and 18:26, but 18:2 has 'Aquila... and his wife Priscilla', and Paul himself writes 'Aquila and Prisca' in 1 Corinthians 16:19. The pattern is real but not uniform.
- The video's reading of 16:7 says Andronicus and Junia are 'well known to the apostles'; the LSB has 'outstanding to the apostles'. The wording is debated (see Where scholars differ).

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. What does the list of names in Romans 16 show about what the gospel produces?
2. How do you tell a sincere brother who disagrees from a divisive deceiver?
3. What voices are you giving access to your mind and community?
4. What fruit does the content you consume produce in you?
5. How are you guarding the garden of your church, to work it and keep it?

## Application
- (video) Paul did not write with social media in mind, but the internet did not invent division, self-interest or flattering speech; it amplifies and rewards them. First-century influencers moved through house churches, patronage circles and traveling teachers; today it is clips, podcasts, posts and comment sections: a different method, the same spiritual pattern. 'The algorithm doesn't care if Christians become holy. It only cares that they stay engaged.' Not every online critic is wrong: ask whether a voice is faithful, careful, accountable and aiming at repentance and restoration, or self-serving, flattering and faction-making. Watch for language like 'only I am telling you the truth', 'every church is corrupt', 'share this before it gets taken down'. Jesus says false teachers are known by their fruits (Matthew 7:15-20). The teacher is accountable to his local church, pastor and discipleship group, and asks the same of others. Online attention is a form of hospitality, so sometimes obedience means unsubscribing, not sharing, not joining the comment war. He keeps social media off his phone. His Romans 16 test for any voice, including his: Are they anchored in Scripture and careful with it? Do they build up the church? Do they show self-interest or need enemies? Are they accountable? What fruit does their content produce in me?
- Study note (added): run the video's Romans 16 test on the three voices you listen to most this week, and write down the fruit each one produces in you. Then thank God by name for three people in your own church, as Paul does in 16:1-16.
